name: loss of social status
description: The sense that you have fallen in the estimation of an important social group.

variations.name: unexpected status loss
variations.description: If you didn't see the loss coming, there may be added senses of surprise, resentment, or injustice.

variations.name: expected status loss
variations.description: Even a pending threat of losing status can create anxiety.

variations.name: economic status loss
variations.description: If you're concerned about getting food to the table, there may be survival-based anxiety or panic.

variations.name: banishment
variations.description: Being cast out of a job or social group is likely to trigger shame, fear, or anger. In ancient times, being an outcast would have been been a survival-level problem.

commentaries.quote: The loss of status is a special case of 'losing' in general. It's highlighted here because for most of us, it's our most important asset. Even money is less important because at least you can couch surf if you have friends.
Even though a loss of status in the modern world is rarely going to kill us, it still triggers deep instincts and brain chemicals meant to keep us tied to the safety of the group.

conditions: The sense that you have fallen in the estimation of an important social group.
